chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Billie Holiday at the Uptown House: Mildred Bailey, Jimmie Monroe and heavy drugs
summary: Collins says Mildred Bailey admired Billie, who resented her; Jimmie Monroe allegedly started her on heroin, and Joe Guy followed, which Collins saw on the West Coast.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Well, I think you mentioned her. We're talking about Mildred Bailey.

Well, one thing, it was just a funny incident I was thinking about. Mildred loved Billie but Billie always had a thing against Mildred because evidently Billie's mother worked for Mildred at one time. I don't know as a maid or as a cook or something, you know. And Billie -- and I think Billie always resented this, you know. But Mildred loved Billie's singing, and used to go up to the Uptown House quite often, because she knew that Billie would be there.

Billie Holiday, yes. Naturally, is there any other singer? Yeah, would go up there to hear her. You know, she knew she would be in. And everybody would go up there. It was quite a place, you know. And as a matter of

fact, Billie as you know -- I don't know whether she married Monroe's brother or they were just living together, but he was the one allegedly who started her on dope, you know. And all the musicians hated him, you know. But he had been in Europe and I think the war drove him back to New York. And she fell in love with this guy, he was a very handsome guy, but obviously a pimp, you know.
It's so -- it's just funny how the singers, the black singers at that time were just attracted to these hustlers and pimps. I just can't imagine why. But --

Who else? Well, most of the singers during that time were, you know, but any way, we were talking about Billie. But Jimmie Monroe, he came back and we noticed that Billie had -- we all smoked pot, but Billie had graduated and she just got away from us. Because she kind of like belonged to us or we belonged to her, I don't know. Kenny Edison Clarke, Sonny White, Freddy Greene, me, Harry Addison. You know, we all loved her, we all kind of felt very close to her, we'd protect her, you know.

And she got away from us through this, so everybody hated Jimmie Monroe because of what he had done to her. Then she and Joe Guy got together, he was a trumpet player, as I told you, and I really believe that she started Joe Guy on the heavy stuff, because I saw Joe later, when I told you that

I recorded with them in San Francisco, and he was obviously on the heavy stuff then, and -- which eventually killed him. So during this time, coming back to the Uptown House, this was something new, you know, because heavy dope at that time was kind of unusual. We, you know, like cocaine and heroin, we really knew nothing about that. We only smoked pot, see.
So it was kind of new, and especially when I came out of the army and I saw all of the musicians using heroin and cocaine I just couldn't understand it.
